gen-gf-paprika-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara draws every curve with a stroke that never swells, leaving generous gaps at the terminals. Hind Vadodara over Paprika's loud, wide-standing lowercase reads smoothly, a sans that lets the heading do the shouting.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-huninn: Huninn looks bent from wire, its lowercase rising close to cap height and its crossbars as fat as the stems. Paprika's scattered, headline-ready letters sit above it, giving the pair a bold front and tidy back.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-inter-tight: Rope-like lines, tight and modern. Paprika shows off with lowercase that fills the line like capitals, while Inter Tight keeps its short ascenders and held-back curve tails quietly in order.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-karla: Karla reads stocky and friendly, with a gaping c and a middle band so tall the line looks packed. Karla feels homely next to Paprika's commanding, hollow-reed counters, like a chatty neighbor beside a loud announcer.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-kedebideri: Paprika arrives loud, its lowercase filling the line like capitals. Kedebideri follows in a sans with a skyward x-height and rounded letters that stay open, so the showy top gives way to a welcoming, easygoing text.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-khula: Big, brash letters with room to spare, scattered wide and standing tall. Khula's brush-pen belly and open-mouthed curves hold the text, while Paprika earns its keep when big and brief.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-krub: Krub stands tall, with a pronounced x-height. Paprika brings the swagger of wide-spaced, capital-sized lowercase, and Krub's pen-lifted curves, left unfinished at the loop, give the pair its strongest quality: a loud voice beside a light touch.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-lexend: Paprika's lowercase swells to fill the line like capitals, hollow-reed counters breathing wide. Lexend, a sans-serif with outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve, offers flat, contrast-free letters that make the pair a study in loud versus level.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca keeps a plain, unshaded line that never swells. Across a long stretch its big lowercase and small-looking capitals feel easy, with terminals stopping short of curling in, a quiet foil to Paprika's commanding display.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-liter: Marker-tip letters meet a bold show-off. Paprika earns its keep when big and short, its capital-sized lowercase commanding attention, while Liter, a sans-serif with no stroke contrast and wide mouths on its rounds, stays tall and sturdy beneath.
